frontPage.headline: Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
frontPage.summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. The company said the board had received input from senior levels of the United States government.
frontPage.whyItMatters: The government's role in a chipmaker's leadership decision is a new kind of dependency for anyone planning around Nvidia's roadmap and supply.

frontPage.headline: Tech stocks rally after Nvidia board approves Jensen Huang's return as CEO
frontPage.summary: CNBC reports that tech stocks rallied after the board approved Huang's return. The Nasdaq had slid 10% the previous week, its worst week since the early days of Covid in 2020.
frontPage.whyItMatters: A single personnel decision reversing a sector-wide selloff shows how concentrated AI infrastructure sentiment has become.

frontPage.headline: Cybersecurity stocks have been hot — and now CrowdStrike inks deal to buy Zscaler
frontPage.summary: CrowdStrike said it will acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction that values Zscaler at approximately $43.9 billion.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Combining endpoint and cloud-access security under one vendor would change platform choices for teams designing zero-trust architectures.

frontPage.headline: Norway says hackers exploited Microsoft security flaw to attack energy firms Equinor, Skagerak Energi
frontPage.summary: Norway's cybersecurity authorities said Equinor and Skagerak Energi were affected by a Microsoft cloud vulnerability that hackers exploited to target sensitive credentials.
frontPage.whyItMatters: A flaw in a managed cloud control-plane service exposes credentials across tenants, which is the failure mode cloud security reviews should assume.

frontPage.headline: Trump says he won't allow US companies to build datacenters abroad
frontPage.summary: President Trump threatened a 'tremendous tax' on US companies that build data centers abroad. The Register notes that analysts question how such restrictions would work.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Siting rules for data centers would constrain how multi-region and data-residency architectures can be built and priced.

frontPage.headline: Microsoft mega outage: Report reveals testing gaps and emails that never arrived
frontPage.summary: A report on Microsoft's large outage describes testing gaps and emails that never arrived. A July bug overwhelmed newer servers, and Microsoft promised stronger safeguards and faster recovery.
frontPage.whyItMatters: The account is a useful case of a latent bug surfacing under a rollout, which is worth checking against your own canary and rollback practice.

frontPage.headline: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
frontPage.summary: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency warned federal agencies that attackers are now exploiting a recently patched critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability in the wild.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Internet-facing collaboration gateways are a common entry point, so patch status there deserves priority.

frontPage.headline: Anthropic Committed to Spend $900 Billion. Wall Street Expects Its Debt to Be Junk.
frontPage.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that after a turbulent IPO, Anthropic's credit rating will affect its capital plans, and Wall Street expects its debt to be rated junk.
frontPage.whyItMatters: The cost of financing at that scale bears on how fast frontier-model capacity, and the GPU orders behind it, can grow.

items.headline: Nvidia’s stock soars 30%-plus as Jensen Huang returns as CEO
items.summary: Nvidia's stock rose on Monday by the most in a decade after the decision to reinstate Huang as president and chief executive.

items.headline: Wall Street's 'Fear Gauge' just flashed a buy sign
items.summary: CNBC reports that Friday's large spike in the VIX could signal a buying opportunity, if history is any guide.

items.headline: Tokenized stocks face pushback as NYSE, Nasdaq pivot for a new market
items.summary: A new tokenized-securities venue, OKXICE, is set to debut Monday despite objections from 90% of the companies whose stocks it initially proposed to list.

items.headline: Gold Rebounds After Sharpest Weekly Decline Since March
items.summary: Gold prices surged nearly 5%, extending earlier gains after the steepest weekly decline since March, as markets rebounded on Nvidia's reinstatement of Huang.

items.headline: Spain approves decree on data centers to curb electricity costs
items.summary: Spain's government approved a decree on data centers aimed at curbing electricity costs, after several months of debate with companies in the sector.

items.headline: FERC approves MISO plan to speed legacy interconnection study process
items.summary: FERC approved a MISO plan to speed its legacy interconnection study process. MISO said that without the changes, queue cycles totaling about 125 GW of generation and storage would have been delayed.

items.headline: SpaceX’s subsidiary Cursor tells lawmakers it's considering phasing out Chinese AI models
items.summary: SpaceX's Cursor told lawmakers it is considering phasing out Chinese-developed open-weight AI models over geopolitical risk, according to a House report reviewed by CNBC.

items.headline: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices
items.summary: GL.iNet confirmed that hackers exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management service to install custom malware on customers' routers and KVM devices. Some users reported backdoors and reverse shells.

items.headline: Cleverbridge warns hackers stole credit card numbers, CVVs in data breach
items.summary: Payments platform Cleverbridge warned that hackers breached its systems and stole customers' payment card information, including card numbers and CVV codes.

items.headline: How Bee implemented Zero Operator Access for personal AI on AWS
items.summary: Bee, an Amazon company, built a personal AI wearable with no mechanism for operators to reach customer data. It uses EC2 instance attestation and the AWS Nitro System to do so.

items.headline: Risky Bulletin: Security products start moving out of the Windows kernel
items.summary: Risky Business reports that security products are starting to move out of the Windows kernel. The bulletin also notes further government network compromises, including the FBI and the US Department of Agriculture.

items.headline: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Harness Is the New Operating System
items.summary: At QCon San Francisco, Manju Rajashekhar argued that the harness around an AI model, not the model itself, decides what an agent can do and how safely. He mapped context, tools, state, permissions and feedback loops onto jobs operating systems already perform.

items.headline: Netflix at QConSF 2026: Retrofitting the SDLC for AI Coding Agents
items.summary: Netflix's Commerce team retrofitted its development lifecycle for AI coding agents. It wrote 45 architecture decision records for people and agents, added a review agent that posts only verified blockers, and serves per-domain GraphRAG context through a single MCP tool.

items.headline: Agoda Reduces API Code Review Time by 64% with Modular Architecture
items.summary: Agoda introduced a modular monolith framework in its post-booking API to cut coupling without a full rewrite. Framework-backed changes showed 64% shorter median code reviews and 34% faster initial feedback than legacy changes.

items.headline: Probing DNS at Cloudflare
items.summary: Cloudflare describes how it extended its internal testing framework to build test tooling for networking protocols, using DNS as the example.

items.headline: Opinion: If the AI bubble bursts, it could create a serious problem for health care
items.summary: A STAT opinion piece by David Adler argues that a health AI company's market value and the medical value of its technology are two different things.

items.headline: Morning Headlines 11/23/26
items.summary: HIStalk reports that Kaiser Permanente researchers found existing electronic health record data can help train AI models to identify first-trimester patients at higher risk of pregnancy complications.

items.headline: Monday Morning Update 11/23/26
items.summary: HIStalk reports that Banner Health is investing in clinical registry software developer Layer Health and will consolidate and automate its registry program with the vendor's technology.

items.headline: Microsoft’s Brad Smith on Trump’s data center tax threat: ‘You can’t support Helsinki from New Jersey’
items.summary: Microsoft President Brad Smith responded to the data center tax threat, saying most data centers must be close to their customers. GeekWire says he also addressed Microsoft's ballroom commitment and reported ByteDance talks.

items.headline: Beyond Nvidia: Convoy co-founder and former Microsoft leader raise $277M to rethink AI infrastructure
items.summary: Marlowe, a new startup from Convoy co-founder Dan Lewis and former Microsoft AI leader Kutta Srinivasan, raised $277 million in seed funding at a $1.15 billion valuation. It will run AI on infrastructure tuned for specific models, with its first site live in December.

items.headline: Etzioni on AI: The outage conspiracy theories are wrong — our rush to patch and upgrade is the culprit
items.summary: Oren Etzioni argues in GeekWire that this month's outages at Microsoft, the FAA, Chase, Apple and the NSA were not a coordinated attack. He says each traces to its own bug, patch or upgrade.

items.headline: Asian Regulators Step Up Efforts to Calm AI-Driven Market Turmoil
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that regulators and market operators in China, South Korea and Taiwan rolled out emergency measures to arrest turmoil from the global rout in AI stocks.

items.headline: U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair
items.summary: The New York Times reports that US intelligence is said to show Alice Huang was in touch with China's Ministry of State Security while in a relationship with Jensen Huang.

items.headline: U.S. probes Megaspeed, Alice Huang as new figure emerges in Nvidia chip case
items.summary: CNBC reports the US is investigating Megaspeed and Alice Huang after a former associate of hers was reportedly deeply involved in the firm's activities.

items.headline: Ukraine Sinks Russian Warship, Hits Cargo Vessels Far From Warzone
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports Ukraine sank a Russian warship and hit cargo vessels far from the war zone, the latest in a series of drone strikes on Russian vessels.

items.headline: Five takeaways from the failed climate talks COP31
items.summary: BBC News lists five takeaways from the failed COP31 climate talks in Antalya, the longest-running in UN history.

items.headline: IRDAI forms expert panel on distribution, commission reforms
items.summary: India's insurance regulator IRDAI formed an expert panel on distribution and commission reforms. It will recommend transition pathways, including phased implementation, to address concerns of smaller insurers and distributors.

items.headline: Nasscom seeks three-Year AI Transformation Scheme in Budget 2027-28
items.summary: Nasscom asked for a three-year AI Transformation Scheme in Budget 2027-28, saying new AI delivery models need heavy upfront investment from startups and MSMEs before returns arrive.

items.headline: Barrier-less tolling offers NHAI a revenue boost
items.summary: Mint reports that barrier-less tolling offers NHAI a revenue boost, with NHAI preparing to invite bids for hundreds of additional plazas.

items.headline: India announces ₹15k-cr package for Nepal as PM Shah wraps up maiden visit
items.summary: India announced a development cooperation package for Nepal, aimed at reconstruction after the devastating floods in August and at improving its capacity to deal with future disasters.

items.headline: Fragments: November 20
items.summary: Martin Fowler relays an experiment finding that healthy code is cheaper for AI agents to review: between a typical unhealthy and a typical healthy pull request the saving is 22 to 35%. It covered three LLMs and 465 pull requests on 246 open source repositories.

items.headline: Shipping 100+ PRs to production in a week
items.summary: Will Larson describes shipping 100+ pull requests to production in a week, reaching 115 in the week of November 9th, mostly written on Imprint's internal cloud harness.

items.headline: The Explorer Pattern for product invention and development.
items.summary: Larson's Explorer Pattern has one person or team build a working implementation with minimal cross-team impact, then reconcile details with other teams afterwards, accepting that this can require substantial rework.

learn.title: Replaying failure on purpose
learn.body:
Distributed systems are hard to test because partial failures overlap with live traffic, and the same fault can produce a different execution trace on every run. A test that fails once in a thousand runs is nearly useless, because you cannot reproduce it, and so you cannot confirm a fix.

Deterministic simulation testing, as Unmesh Joshi describes it in Martin Fowler's collection of articles, attacks the problem by removing the sources of nondeterminism. The real clock, the real network and the real storage are replaced with simulated components. All of them are driven by one single-threaded execution loop. Because nothing runs in parallel and nothing reads real time, the whole run is a function of its starting inputs. If a run fails, running it again with the same inputs reproduces the failure exactly.

The simulation can then do things a live cluster cannot do on demand. It can inject hard failures such as a crashed node or a dropped link. It can also inject the routine slowdowns that often cause real incidents, such as network and disk latency spikes, and it can do so at the exact step where the protocol is most fragile. Since simulated time costs nothing, a test can cover hours or days of cluster behaviour in seconds, and run many thousands of differently seeded schedules overnight.

A concrete case: consider a leader election protocol with a lease. In the simulator, you let a node pause just past its lease expiry while a message from its successor is delayed. If two nodes ever believe they are leader, the run fails, and its seed becomes a regression test you keep.

What to take into a design: build the component interfaces for time, network and storage from the start, so a simulator can stand in for them later. Retrofitting is possible but costly. Keep the core logic single-threaded or schedulable by an external loop. Treat every failing seed as a permanent test. Be aware of the limits: the simulator only finds bugs in the behaviours you modelled, so it complements, rather than replaces, tests on real hardware and failure drills in production. This note is based on the article's summary; the full page could not be opened today, so details beyond the summary are the editor's framing of the technique.
